result.summary:
Read docs/agents/design/REQ-020.md in full myself (not CODE-DESIGNER's step-01-code-designer.json result.summary). The correctness-critical content is sound and I confirmed it independently: the FOR UPDATE row-lock mechanism (S1.1-1.3) is a genuinely correct fix for S7's exact race, the S8/AC7 audit-row reading is the correct resolution, qr_token generation is a real CSPRNG at well over the 128-bit floor, the source/pending_source reuse matches the actual domain/event.ts signatures, PgSelectBuilder.for() is a real typed Drizzle 0.45.2 method, and all 7 ACs map to concrete design elements. But the zero-implementation-code check -- which this gate applies with no partial credit -- finds two real executable code fragments, not signatures/types, so this FAILs on that check alone.

1. FOR UPDATE race trace (independently re-derived, not taken from S1.1's prose): Event has capacity N, N-1 already admitted (1 seat left). Tx A: SELECT...FOR UPDATE events row -> acquires exclusive row lock. Tx B (concurrent): SELECT...FOR UPDATE same row -> blocks, cannot proceed past its own step 2 (S3.2), because Postgres makes a second FOR UPDATE waiter block on an already-locked row rather than let it read past the lock. Tx A continues under the held lock: counts admitted=N-1, computeSeatsLeft=1>0, decides 'admitted', INSERTs the registration row, writes the audit_log row, commits -> releases the lock. Tx B's blocked SELECT...FOR UPDATE now unblocks, acquires the lock, and (per READ COMMITTED's per-statement snapshot) its own subsequent countAdmittedRegistrations issues a fresh SELECT that sees Tx A's now-committed INSERT: count=N, computeSeatsLeft=0, decides 'waitlisted'. Result: exactly one admission for the last seat, never two. Confirmed this genuinely requires FOR UPDATE specifically: at READ COMMITTED with no lock at all, both transactions' SELECT COUNT statements can execute concurrently before either has committed its INSERT -- each would independently observe count=N-1, each would independently compute seatsLeft=1>0, and both would insert 'admitted', overrunning capacity by one. This is exactly S7's stated negative case ('two concurrent registrations for the last seat both admitted'). The lock is what forces the second transaction's read to happen strictly after the first transaction's write commits, not merely inside a transaction boundary alone. This part of the design is correct and matches its own stated reasoning.

2. Verified PgSelectBuilder.for(strength, config?) is a real method: node_modules/drizzle-orm/pg-core/query-builders/select.d.ts line 586 confirms `for(strength: LockStrength, config?: LockConfig): PgSelectWithout<this, TDynamic, 'for'>;` in the installed drizzle-orm 0.45.2 (node_modules/drizzle-orm/package.json). The design's claim in S1.2 is accurate, not asserted-but-unverified.

3. S8/AC7 audit-row resolution (S6, flagged as open question 4 in S9): I confirm CODE-DESIGNER's reading, not just accept it on its own say-so. AC7's text ('each admission writes exactly one audit_log row') is the narrower, illustrative acceptance case; security-invariants.md S8 ('every status change writes exactly one AuditLog row') is the broader, authoritative gate rule this workflow's Step 2c will actually check against. A registrations row moving from non-existent to 'waitlisted' is a status change under S8's own wording -- there is no textual carve-out in S8 for waitlisting. Per core-directives.md's precedence rule ('a safety/gate rule is never overridden by a more specific instruction'), S8's broader wording governs; AC7's narrower phrasing does not license omitting the waitlisted-outcome audit row. Writing exactly one audit_log row on both 'admitted' and 'waitlisted' (S3.2 step 8f) satisfies AC7 literally (admissions still get exactly one row) while fully satisfying S8. This is settled, not reopened for Step 2c to re-litigate -- SECURITY-REVIEWER should verify the mechanism holds in the actual implementation, not re-decide the reading.

4. qr_token (S4, AC3): generateQrToken (S4) is specified as node:crypto's randomBytes(32) (256 bits) hex-encoded -- a real CSPRNG, well over S4's >=128-bit floor. Confirmed no Math.random, counter, or hash-of-userId path exists anywhere else in the design (grepped the design doc text myself: 'Math.random' appears exactly once, inside S4.2's own sentence stating it is never used). registrations.qr_token's existing uniqueIndex (REQ-011, unchanged) is the correct durable backstop; the no-retry-on-collision gap is honestly flagged as open question 3, not silently assumed away.

5. source/pending_source integration (S5, AC5): read apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts myself. getPendingSource(db, userId): Promise<string|null> (lines 687-693ish) and setPendingSource(db, userId, channel): Promise<void> (lines 679-685) match exactly what S3.2 step 8a and S5.2's clearPendingSource mirror. resolveRegistrationSource's prose rule (pendingSource ?? 'direct', stated without executable syntax) is a correct, complete description of the fallback the requirement needs.

6. Reuse verification: computeSeatsLeft(capacity, admittedCount), isRegistrationOpen(registrationClosesAt, evaluationTime), isFinished(endsAt, evaluationTime), countAdmittedRegistrations(db, eventId), getEventByIdWithChapterTimezone -- all read directly from apps/bot/src/domain/event.ts, all match the design's stated call shapes and signatures exactly (no invented parameter, no signature drift).

7. AC map (S11): all 7 ACs map to a named, concrete design element; no 'TBD' or deferral language anywhere in the document; every open question (S9, six items) is named explicitly rather than silently resolved.

8. Zero-implementation-code check -- FAILS here, and this gate has no partial credit:
   - Line 388: `export const REGISTER_CALLBACK_PATTERN = /^register:(.+)$/;` is a concrete runtime value (a regex literal assigned to an exported const), not a type or a bare function signature. Every other declaration in this document that is design-legitimate ends a *signature* in ';' with no value (export function/export async function/export interface/export type). This line supplies the actual value BACKEND-DEV would otherwise have had to choose and write -- copy-pasteable verbatim into the implementation.
   - Line 437: `new InlineKeyboard().text(catalog.registration.registerButton, \`register:${event.id}\`)` is a real, executable object-construction expression with a template-literal interpolation -- not a signature, not a type, not prose. It is the literal working code for the reply_markup value, presented as a code fragment rather than described the way S7.1's numbered steps and S2.2's decision table describe everything else in this same document (in prose, with no executable syntax). code-designer.md's rule ('applies just as much to bot/backend logic... A function with a real if/return/arithmetic/comparison statement in its body... is implementation, full stop, regardless of how trivial the logic looks') is stated in terms of function bodies, but the underlying principle -- no copy-pasteable working code, however trivial -- is violated by both lines equally: these are not function bodies, but they are the same category of 'obviously fine because it's trivial' concrete code that caused REQ-016 and REQ-017 to FAIL this exact check twice before. The rest of this document (S2.2's outcome table, S3.2's ordered prose steps, S7.1's ordered prose steps) demonstrates CODE-DESIGNER already knows how to state this content without executable syntax; these two lines are the only departures from that discipline in an otherwise disciplined document.

Rework instructions for CODE-DESIGNER: rewrite S7.1's REGISTER_CALLBACK_PATTERN reference and S7.3's InlineKeyboard construction as prose (e.g. 'the callback pattern recognizes callback_data of the shape register:<eventId>, following the exact convention CHAPTER_CALLBACK_PATTERN already establishes in handlers/start.ts' and 'the reply_markup is an inline keyboard with exactly one button: label sourced from catalog.registration.registerButton, callback data register:<eventId>'). No other section requires rework -- S1-S6, S8-S11 all passed every check independently re-derived above.

issues.description: docs/agents/design/REQ-020.md line 388 (`export const REGISTER_CALLBACK_PATTERN = /^register:(.+)$/;`) and line 437 (`new InlineKeyboard().text(catalog.registration.registerButton, \`register:${event.id}\`)`) are concrete, copy-pasteable executable code -- a literal regex value and a real object-construction expression -- not type/signature-only design content. Rewrite both as prose, matching the discipline already used everywhere else in this document (S2.2's table, S3.2/S7.1's ordered prose steps).
